title: Detect a jit binary that predates the repository it is validating
description:
Gate checkers invoke `jit` from `PATH`, not the binary built from the working tree. After a change to storage, validation, or any command a checker calls, the gate silently exercises the previously installed binary. The gate result then describes a version of the product that is not the one under review.

Observed twice while driving epic 004d10b7. In the worst case `scripts/jit-validate.sh` (`exec jit validate "$@"`) reported an issue as not found using a stale binary; the `code-review` gate reported that as a blocking finding against the change under review, and the round was spent chasing a defect that did not exist in the working tree. The workaround is to remember `cargo install --path crates/jit` after landing anything a checker touches — a step nothing prompts for and whose omission produces a plausible-looking failure rather than an obvious one.

## The mechanism, and why the fix is cheap

The binary already knows both halves of the comparison. `crates/jit/build_info.rs` (populated by `crates/jit/build.rs`) embeds the commit it was built from and whether that tree was dirty; `jit --version` prints them:

    jit 0.2.1 (commit 824a4e74, dirty=true, profile release)

So a running `jit` can compare the commit it was built from against the repository's current `HEAD` and tell the operator that it is judging a tree it was not built from. Nothing does this today.

Every repo-local gate checker in `scripts/` shells out to `jit` this way (`jit-validate.sh`, `docs-mechanical.sh`, `docs-check-projections.sh`, `docs-check-citations.sh`, and others), so the exposure is the whole gate surface, not one script.

Decide, with reasons, between warning and failing: a warning keeps a legitimate cross-version run possible; a hard failure inside a gate context is defensible because a gate verdict from the wrong binary is not evidence about the change. A `--allow-stale-binary` style escape hatch, or scoping the check to gate runs, are both acceptable resolutions if justified.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: When the running binary was built from a commit other than the repository's current `HEAD` (or from a dirty tree that no longer matches), jit surfaces that fact rather than silently proceeding; the chosen behavior (warn or fail) is justified against the gate-evidence argument above.
- [hard] REQ-02: The check reaches the gate path, so a checker cannot return a verdict from a binary that predates the tree under review without that being visible in the run record.
- [hard] REQ-03: The check does not fire for an ordinary user running an installed release against an unrelated repository, and does not require git (`@/charter/D-4`): outside a git repository, or with no resolvable HEAD, it stays silent.
- [hard] REQ-04: Coverage exercises both the matching and mismatching cases against the real build-info values.
